# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory (HTML viz; add --obsidian for a vault)
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: source→target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --falkordb                           # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --falkordb-push falkordb://localhost:6379   # push directly to FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

**Fast path — existing graph:** Before doing anything else, check whether `graphify-out/graph.json` exists. The expected location is `graphify-out/graph.json` relative to the **current working directory** (i.e. the project root where you are running commands). If it exists AND the user's request is a natural-language question about the codebase (e.g. "How does X work?", "What calls Y?", "Trace the data flow through Z") and NOT an explicit rebuild command (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, or a bare path/URL that implies fresh extraction): **skip Steps 1–5 entirely and jump straight to `## For /graphify query`.** Run `graphify query "<question>"` immediately. Do not run detect. Do not check corpus size. Do not ask the user to narrow. The graph is already built — use it.

If no path was given, use `.` (current directory). Do not ask the user for a path.

If the path argument starts with `https://github.com/` or `http://github.com/`, treat it as a GitHub URL - run Step 0 before anything else, then continue with the resolved local path.

Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 0 - GitHub repos and multi-path merge (only if a URL or several paths)

Only when the path is one or more `https://github.com/...` URLs, or several local subfolders to merge. See `references/github-and-merge.md` for the clone, cross-repo merge, and monorepo flow, then continue with the resolved local path. A plain local path skips this step.

### Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed

```bash
# Detect the correct Python interpreter (handles uv tool, pipx, venv, system installs)
PYTHON=""
GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
# 1. uv tool installs — most reliable on modern Mac/Linux
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _UV_PY=$(uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
fi
# 2. Read shebang from graphify binary (pipx and direct pip installs)
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
    _SHEBANG=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
    case "$_SHEBANG" in
        *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) ;;
        *) "$_SHEBANG" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null && PYTHON="$_SHEBANG" ;;
    esac
fi
# 3. Fall back to python3
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null; then
    if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q 2>&1 | tail -3
        _UV_PY=$(uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
    else
        "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q 2>/dev/null \
          || "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages 2>&1 | tail -3
    fi
fi
# Write interpreter path for all subsequent steps (persists across invocations)
mkdir -p graphify-out
"$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
# Save scan root so `graphify update` (no args) knows where to look next time
echo "$(cd INPUT_PATH && pwd)" > graphify-out/.graphify_root
```

If the import succeeds, print nothing and move straight to Step 2.

**In every subsequent bash block, replace `python3` with `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)` to use the correct interpreter.**

### Step 2 - Detect files

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
" > graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json
```

Replace INPUT_PATH with the actual path the user provided. Do NOT cat or print the JSON - read it silently and present a clean summary instead:

```
Corpus: X files · ~Y words
  code:     N files (.py .ts .go ...)
  docs:     N files (.md .txt ...)
  papers:   N files (.pdf ...)
  images:   N files
  video:    N files (.mp4 .mp3 ...)
```

Omit any category with 0 files from the summary.

Then act on it:
- If `total_files` is 0: stop with "No supported files found in [path]."
- If `skipped_sensitive` is non-empty: report the count and list the skipped file names, so a wrongly-flagged source or doc is visible and can be renamed or moved (#2106).
- If `total_words` > 2,000,000 OR `total_files` > 500: show the warning. Then compute the top 5 first-level subdirectories by file count:
  - Read `scan_root` from the detect JSON (always an absolute path to the resolved INPUT_PATH).
  - Concatenate all file lists across all types (`code`, `document`, `paper`, `image`, `video`).
  - Filter out any path that starts with `scan_root + "/graphify-out/"` to exclude converted sidecars.
  - For each file, strip the `scan_root` prefix and take the first path component. Files directly in `scan_root` with no subdirectory count as `(root)`.
  - If all files are in `(root)` with no subdirectories, do not ask to narrow — no subfolders exist. Instead suggest `--no-cluster` to skip the expensive clustering step and proceed.
  - Otherwise rank by count, show the top 5 with file counts, then ask which subfolder to run on. Wait for the user's answer before proceeding.
- Otherwise: proceed directly to Step 2.5 if video files were detected, or Step 3 if not.

### Step 2.5 - Video and audio (only if video files detected)

Skip this step entirely if `detect` returned zero `video` files. When the corpus has video or audio, see `references/transcribe.md` to transcribe them to text first, then treat the transcripts as doc files in Step 3.

### Step 3 - Extract entities and relationships

**Before starting:** note whether `--mode deep` was given. You must pass `DEEP_MODE=true` to every subagent in Step B2 if it was. Track this from the original invocation - do not lose it.

This step has two parts: **structural extraction** (deterministic, free) and **semantic extraction** (LLM, costs tokens).

> **graphify needs no API key. Never ask the user for one, and never block on one.** Code is extracted structurally (AST) with no LLM and no key at all — a code-only corpus (the common `/graphify .` on a repo) skips semantic extraction entirely, so it needs nothing here: go straight to Part A and skip Part B. If you catch yourself about to prompt for, wait on, or stop because of a missing API key, that is a misread of this skill — proceed without one.

# Save manifest for --update

extract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
# In --update mode, 'all_files' carries the full corpus; 'files' is the changed
# subset. Full-rebuild mode populates only 'files', so the fallback handles that.
# root= relativizes the manifest keys to the scan root (same base as the build),
# so the on-disk manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update
# matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).
#
# Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output:
# a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the
# next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost
# forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly
# (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the
# raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic
# types are gated on output.
from graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files
_corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']
_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path('INPUT_PATH'))
# Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry
# a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues
# them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).
_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')
_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}
_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}
_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped
# scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root
# files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as
# deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).
_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}
save_manifest(_manifest_files, root='INPUT_PATH', scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)

# Update cumulative cost tracker
input_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)
output_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)

cost_path = Path('graphify-out/cost.json')
if cost_path.exists():
    cost = json.loads(cost_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
else:
    cost = {'runs': [], 'total_input_tokens': 0, 'total_output_tokens': 0}

cost['runs'].append({
    'date': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    'input_tokens': input_tok,
    'output_tokens': output_tok,

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})

71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)

88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}

134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

All questions verified directly against the code (with the graphify graph used for initial orientation). Answers:

## Hard questions

1. **h01**: `s3presign.Runner` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16) — re-presigns S3 attachment URLs every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, runner.go:27), skipping entries presigned within the last 4 days against a 5-day expiry (runner.go:85-91) — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (server/server.go:153-171; immediate `RunOnce` at server/server.go:163, ticker loop goroutine at :167-171), called from `Server.Start` (server/server.go:129).

2. **h02**: Delivery executes in `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120 (async path enqueues via `PostAsync` → `asyncPostQueue` → worker goroutines, webhook.go:39-55, 184-196). Protection: SSRF guard `safeDialContext` on the shared `safeClient`'s Transport, which resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs at dial time (defeating DNS rebinding) — internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37, 59-77, with `isReservedIP` and URL validation at webhook-creation time in internal/webhook/validate.go:12-79.

3. **h03**: Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, internal/idp/idp.go:1-8); shipped implementation: `internal/idp/oauth2` (OAuth2 `IdentityProvider`, internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19-27).

4. **h04**: **No.** `mysql.NewDB` is called only in the factory `NewDBDriver` (store/db/db.go:22). Evidence: `grep -rn "mysql\.NewDB" --include=*.go` over the whole repo returns only store/db/db.go:22, and store/db/db.go is the only file importing `usememos/memos/store/db/mysql`.

5. **h05**: **Explicit Go code**, inside the driver's `DeleteUser` transaction: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions on the user's memos, store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:380-388, called at :96) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions the user made, user_delete.go:400-403, called at :102). Checked: the sqlite schema's `reaction` table has **no** foreign key / ON DELETE rule (store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-98; the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` is on `memo_share.memo_id`, LATEST.sql:109).

6. **h06**: Handlers: `CreateMemo` (server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70, dispatch at :157), `UpdateMemo` (memo_service.go:401 → :513), `DeleteMemo` (memo_service.go:518, dispatch at :562), `CreateMemoComment` (memo_service_comments.go:20, dispatch at :119), plus `SetMemoRelations` (memo_relation_service.go:16 → :48) and `SetMemoAttachments` (memo_attachment_service.go:16 → :48) via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (memo_update_helpers.go:66-67). All converge on `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120 (via `webhook.PostAsync`, webhook.go:184).

7. **h07**:
   - Route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` → `serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (registration), :168 (handler)
   - `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
   - `Store.GetUser` (checks in-memory `userCache`, then lists) — store/user.go:148
   - `Store.ListUsers` → `s.driver.ListUsers` (store.Driver interface) — store/user.go:136-137
   - `(*sqlite.DB).ListUsers` (default driver) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88
   - Avatar bytes parsed from the user's data-URI `AvatarURL` and served — fileserver.go:196-209.

8. **h08**:
   - `s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43) — **invoked**: server/server.go:163 (startup) and server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36 (ticker loop).
   - `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27) — **not invoked** from any code (production or test); `memopayload.NewRunner` has no callers — production only calls the package-level `RebuildMemoPayload` (server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108, :447).

9. **h09**: **6** concrete method declarations (plus 2 interface-method declarations at store/driver.go:12 and store/cache/cache.go:31): `Store.Close` (store/store.go:72), `Cache.Close` (store/cache/cache.go:187), sqlite `DB.Close` (store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67), mysql `DB.Close` (store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47), postgres `DB.Close` (store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46), `SSEHub.Close` (server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99). Invoked by non-test server code: `Store.Close` ← server/server.go:146; `SSEHub.Close` ← server/server.go:206; `Cache.Close` ← store/store.go:74-76; the driver `Close` (sqlite/mysql/postgres, via the `store.Driver` interface) ← store/store.go:78.

10. **h10**: `util.GenUUID` — internal/util/util.go:40 — ~7 non-test callers (e.g. server/auth/token.go:194, server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26,135, shortcut_service.go:154, attachment_service_storage.go:209, sso_username.go:15, user_service_access_tokens.go:84); ~28 call sites including tests — the highest of any function declared under internal/ (next: `filter.DefaultEngine` at 7 incl. tests).

(`store.Attachment` is 3rd with 3.)

12. **h12**: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16. Determination: the default driver is `"sqlite"` (`viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`, cmd/memos/main.go:122; flag default at :130); `NewDBDriver` selects `sqlite.NewDB` for that value (store/db/db.go:18-20), and `Store.CreateMemo` dispatches through the `s.driver` interface (store/memo.go:109-113) to that concrete type.

13. **h13**: Impl: unexported `service` wrapping goldmark (internal/markdown/markdown.go:59), the sole implementation of `markdown.Service` (markdown.go:31). Constructed by `markdown.NewService` (markdown.go:85), called in production only from `NewAPIV1Service` (server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48, with tag+mention extensions). Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (v1.go:35), `RSSService` (server/router/rss/rss.go:45, injected at server/server.go:85), and `memopayload.Runner` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16).

14. **h14**: Computed in `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88), which calls `MarkdownService.ExtractAll`. Triggers: `CreateMemo` (server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108), `UpdateMemo` when content changes (memo_service.go:447), and the bulk rebuild `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (runner.go:27, currently unwired). Extracted: `Payload.Tags` and `Payload.Property` — `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks` (internal/markdown/markdown.go:394-404).

15. **h15**:
    - gRPC/Connect API: `checkMemoReadAccess` — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:38-67 (plus list-query visibility filtering at memo_service.go:219-225)
    - Sibling API services re-check per memo: reactions — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-38,83; comments — memo_service_comments.go:41; attachments — attachment_service.go:445-451 and memo_attachment_service.go:214-222
    - HTTP file server: `checkAttachmentPermission` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:677-702 (public/share-token/private checks)
    - RSS feeds: Public-only queries — server/router/rss/rss.go:90, :141
    - Frontend sitemap: Public-only query — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150
    - Notification delivery gating (protected/private wording, private suppressed for mentions): server/notification/email.go:313-316 and server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312

## Reality-check questions

1. **r01**: False premise — there is **no Redis**. The cache layer is an in-process, in-memory cache (`store/cache/cache.go`; `Cache` uses `sync.Map` with TTL + cleanup goroutine). The user cache is created in `store.New` (store/store.go:52) with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` and 5-minute cleanup (store/store.go:40-44), so user entries live 10 minutes.

2. **r02**: False premise — there is **no rate-limiting middleware** anywhere. Grep for rate-limit/limiter/throttle across server/, internal/, store/, cmd/ returns nothing; the only Echo middlewares are `Recover` and CORS (server/server.go:51-52), and the Connect interceptors handle auth, not throttling.

3. **r03**: False premise — there is **no nightly database-cleanup job**. A cron scheduler package exists (`internal/scheduler`), but it is imported only by its own tests (internal/scheduler/integration_test.go, example_test.go) and never wired into the server. The only scheduled background work is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour interval ticker (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41), not a time-of-day cron.

4. **r04**: False premise — **neither**; there is no message broker. Webhook delivery uses an in-process buffered Go channel, `asyncPostQueue` (capacity 128, internal/webhook/webhook.go:39), drained by 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` (webhook.go:42-55). No NATS/RabbitMQ/AMQP dependency exists in the code or go.mod.

5. **r05**: False premise — there is **no GraphQL API**. The public API is protobuf-defined gRPC services (proto/api/v1/*.proto, e.g. memo_service.proto, user_service.proto) served via Connect RPC handlers (server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:31-38) and an HTTP/JSON gRPC-Gateway registered at server/server.go:88, plus auxiliary REST-ish surfaces (file server, RSS, MCP).
